set.st: The Mount farm near Wyanet was where "old Bulbona" (Bourbonnais), a mixed-blood trader, his Indian wife and children lived and traded with the Indians. Mrs. Mount found a 1786 Spanish silver coin among her plants. A 1928 Princeton paper adds that Gurdon Hubbard, the fur trader, built a house in the grove in 1829 on what was later the J. W. Mount farm. Pin is between the two Mount farms on the 1875 atlas, not the spot itself.
pinev: 1875 Bureau Co atlas, Wyanet Twp T16N R8E: 'J. W. Mount 40' in the NE of sec 29 and 'Wm. Mount 80' on the W edge of sec 28, about 1.5 mi S/SW of Wyanet village; timber stippling runs along the creek E of the village. Pin on the 28/29 line between the two Mount tracts.
Bulbona Grove itself is unlabelled on the 1875 atlas
1905 Bureau atlas (Wyanet Twp p. 31): E. J. Mount 80 in E sec 29 and J. W. Mount 80 in W sec 28, with more Mount lots in secs 20, 30, 32, 33; school NW sec 28; 'Bulbona' not labelled.

Bureau County Tribune, 3 Aug 1928: Hubbard's 1829 house in Bulbona's grove 'on farm now owned by J. W. Mount', but it says Walnut Twp, not Wyanet; the J. W. Mount tracts on the 1875 and 1905 atlases are in Wyanet Twp secs 28-29, so the pin stays there until the Walnut Twp plat page is read.

src: Bureau County Tribune (Princeton), 3 Aug 1928, p. 1 (Hubbard's 1829 house in Bulbona's grove, on the J. W. Mount farm)
